December 2009 ## US chases Asian recovery - Our preliminary data shows that the world’s copper and alloy semis output in Q3 was still 18% below year-ago levels, with alloy rod, bar and section suffering the most severe y-o-y decline in volumes. North East and Developing Asia is undergoing a more rapid recovery in production compared to the rest of the world, supported by a positive momentum driven by improved domestic demand and general restocking activities from the industrial sector. - The outlook for the flat rolled product industry in North America and Asia has improved. Market contacts believe that the US will recover quicker than Europe, partly due to a pick up in automotive sales. Stimulus packages, especially in China and Japan, have proven to be more effective than most expected. #### **Semis output year-on-year comparison by product** 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 12 **December 2009** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com # Plate, sheet, strip and foil ### Chinese output supported by new and

additional capacity 

We have revised up our estimate for Chinese copper plate, sheet, strip, and foil output for Q3 by 5,000t, based on new capacity and a significant increase in Chinese exports from 66,000t in Q2 to 96,000t in Q3. However, the 39% increase in production y-o-y mainly stemmed from new capacity coming on stream in China rather than gains in overseas export markets as more than half of its exports went into Hong Kong. According to CRU’s Beijing analyst, copper and alloy flat rolled product capacity expansion at existing plants in the country amounted to 290,000t per year in 2009, including an additional 100,000t per year of **Chalco Luoyang Copper** (started in July 2009), 100,000t per year of **Chalco Central China Copper** , and 90,000t per year of **Ningbo Xingye Group** .  It is confirmed that **Chalco Shanghai Copper** will also increase its capacity from 60,000t to 120,000t in 2010.    One might doubt at what rate this new capacity will be running at since global flat rolled demand has yet to fully recover.  Nevertheless, market participants are confident that domestic consumption will stay strong in Q4 2009 and throughout 2010. The government has decided to continue rural subsidy programs for electronic products and automobiles, which have been proved effective in supporting demand for high-precision copper and alloy plate, sheet and strip.  We estimate that Chinese copper and alloy flat rolled output in the third quarter of the year totalled 353,000t, which is 55% of Asian output and almost 36% of world output in Q3. 

Elsewhere in Asia, Japanese copper flat rolled output was 65,000t while alloy flat rolled output was 40,000t in Q3.  This was a 40% increase in total volumes from Q2.  The **Japan Copper and Brass Association** said that copper semis output fell by 17% y-o-y to 66,145t in September.  Preliminary data from the association suggested that copper semis output fell again in October but by the slowest rate since last November.  It is therefore predicted that the y-o-y comparisons will be much more favourable in the remainder of the year.  Industry sources hold the view that the Japanese stimulus package has worked well and the market is improving due to better demand in the IT and automotive sectors. South Korea saw similar trends as production increased sequentially during the third quarter. We remain optimistic that the Asian region will experience a much more consistent recovery through to next year benefiting from robust demand in China, compared to North America and Europe. 

### The US market might recover quicker than Europe 

As mentioned above, we are not particularly confident about the North American or the European markets, based on the y-o-y decline in production volumes.  However, volumes recovered slightly during the third quarter.  Q3 copper and alloy plate, sheet, strip and foil output in the US increased by 11% on Q2 but still down 22% y-o-y.  European production in Q3 increased by 12% q-o-q to 2

14,000t, with Germany taking the lead. Market contacts in the two regions also reported that the improvement seen in Q3 in demand for copper and alloy flat rolled products is slowing as downstream industries have begun destocking ahead of extended shutdowns over the Christmas/New Year holidays. Nevertheless, some believe that the US will come out of the recession quicker than Europe because of improving automotive sales as well as the weak US dollar. In November, light vehicle sales in the US totalled 744,669 units, compared to 743,606 units for the same month a year ago, according to data from Ward’s Auto. We hear that there was a pick up in production volumes in Q3 and Q4 in North America but Western Europe is still sluggish. In November, Italian copper and alloy semis producer **KME** said in its quarterly report that it expects Q4 demand will further stabilise as its copper semis products has begun to show signs of bottoming out in Q3. The company is concerned that demand will fall back again next year when the impact from stimulus packages and stock building from rock bottom levels diminishes. **Aurubis** said in December that its flat product output for the fiscal year ended 30th September 2009 declined by more than 30% y-o-y but it expects demand to improve towards the end of 2009 as end use sectors recover. © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 12 **December 2009** Copper and copper alloy mill products **www.crumonitor.com** |Copper plat|e, sh|eet,|strip|and|foil|||||||||||| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |**('000 tonnes)**|||**2007**|||**% Ch**|||**2008**|||**% Ch**||**2009**||**% Ch**| ||**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**

Demand has stabilised at levels 10-15% below that seen before the crisis hit, though there are few signs outside China that there will be a significant pick up in business in the (usually) stronger seasonal first and second quarters of 2011. The uncertain economic climate, coupled with the continued escalation in the copper price and the pressure to keep inventories at a minimum through the supply chain have combined to restrain buying interest. CRU estimates that world market volumes fell by 8% y-o-y in the third quarter of 2009, bringing the cumulative decline back to only 14% for the first three quarters of the year. Our expectation is that Q4 volumes should be higher than last year, if only because conditions in the large Chinese ACR market are now brighter than they were twelve months ago. ### US tube industry splits into two factions over anti-dumping The US tube industry has factionalised into the two camps of those seeking the introduction of antidumping duties on Chinese and Mexican tube imports ( **Mueller Industries, Cerro

Flow Products and Kobe Wieland** ) and those who do not ( **Luvata, Wolverine Tube, Cambridge Lee** ).  The former are clearly fearful that the combination of the new capacity now starting up in Mexico ( **Golden Dragon and Luvata** ) plus continued exports from China will ignite a damaging price war.  Their unilateral decision to seek these duties (as there could be no consensus agreement through the **Copper Brass Fabricators Council** ) is a bold, but inherently controversial move.  Their timing, designed to cause maximum annoyance and aggravation to the new start ups has already led to some fiery statements with claims and counter claims of arguments with greater or lesser merit and legal teams being assembled to represent the interests of the competing parties.  But the anti-dumping petitioners have won the first round with the International Trade Commission casting a 6-0 vote in favour at its preliminary investigation.  A more detailed probe will now take place to assess the magnitude of the alleged “dumping”.  Ultimately, the US Department of Commerce could issue a preliminary determination as early as 9<sup>th</sup> March, 2010, and a final determination as early as 24<sup>th</sup> May, 2010.  Interestingly, there has been some upturn in US tube orders since the action started.  No doubt the war of words will grow in severity and intensity as these dates near. 

### Mixed trends through Asia markets 

There is no sign of an early recovery in Japan and South Korea.  Japanese tube shipments fell 26% y-o-y in September to 8,868t, the fifth month this calendar year that shipments have failed to reach 10,000t. Producer inventories are nominal totalling only 2,261t in September.  Trial shipments of higher strength copper alloy tubes to achieve premium thin walling are now beginning to offset the increase in copper prices.  Volumes are negligible thus far but it will be revealing to await customer feedback.  The South Korean market has also taken a more adverse trend recently.  Production fell from a reasonably healthy 12,193t in September (+14% y-o-y) to only 8,848t in October (-17% y-o-y).  This was in response to a 20% y-o-y slump in October shipments down to only 7,876t.  Meanwhile, producer inventories have climbed to their highest level so far this year (8,246t) suggesting that future production schedules will be restrained.  In China, however, tube production has accelerated due to a sharp recovery in AC output. 

### European markets lower but generally stable 

European copper tube demand has been running around 18% lower this year.  Unusually, tube imports rose to their highest level to date in the third quarter, suggesting that the pattern of sequential recovery was proving stronger than the usual seasonal trend, which we would expect to see in late summer. Consumption seems to be improving at a faster rate in Northern Europe than in the South.  Unfortunately the recent escalation of the copper price back up to around $7,000/t will be

But from a sequential perspective, output was up by 3%, supporting the argument that some segments are in a slow recovery mode. Fabricators responded to the recent modest upturn in the market of alloy rod, bar and section by slightly raising their output. From a regional perspective this positive momentum is mainly driven by North East and Developing Asia. North American production experienced growth whilst European remained flat. From an end-use point of view, we believe that increased demand for alloy rod, bar and section was generated by the industrial sector and some general restocking. As the CRU macroeconomic indices illustrate, world IP grew in Q2 and Q3 by 4.3% and 0.2% q-o-q respectively. ### A mixed, two-speed picture in the Western World Our findings show that alloy rod, bar and section output in the US amounted to 49,000t in Q3. The figure was down by 28% y-o-y but up by 10% from Q2. We estimate that consumption in Q3 amounted to 50,000t. Compared with the same period from last year the figure was down by 30%, however, sequentially consumption rose by 12% as the US economy returned to growth. For Q3 2009 the OEM segment of **Mueller Industries** posted net sales of US$181.6 million compared with US$299.5 million in the same period of 2008. The figure was down by 39% y-o-y, when the average copper price on Comex fell by only 23%. Italian production of alloy rod, bar and section totalled 75,000t in Q3. From a y-o-y point of view, that was a 28% contraction. However, the figure was also down by 9% from the previous quarter, indicating no recovery signs yet. Estimated consumption in Q3 was 71,000t; the figure plunged by 29% y-o-y and was still a 12% contraction from the previous quarter. Italian exports in Q3 grew by 3% q-o-q to 11,000t. Our overall findings suggest that Italy is still suffering badly from the downturn. **KME** said that even though the economy has exhibited some improvement indications, it is still questionable whether this is a solid recovery as it is primarily the government stimuli around the world that provided economic support and boosted demand. The picture in Germany provided some glimmer of hope regarding the widely expected market rebound; although output was down by 20% y-o-y to 41,000t, it was up sequentially by 8%. German exports of alloy rod, bar and section in Q3 totalled 19,000t, down by 30% y-o-y and up by 2% q-o-q. For an export-orientated economy, this figure provides some positive sentiment that the global

economic activity is slowly getting back on track. The recovery in France followed a similar pattern. Production plummeted by 37% y-o-y to 14,000t but rose by 8% q-o-q. ### Asia is leading the way in growth We estimate that Chinese production in Q3 reached 187,000t. The figure exhibited 9% growth compared with the same period of the previous year, supported by the massive government stimulus pack. However, on a sequential basis, output was down by 1%. Chinese consumption in Q3 rose by 11% y-o-y and by 1% q-o-q to 212,000t. Production in North East Asian countries saw the recovery pattern that CRU anticipated earlier this year. Japan was still down in Q3 by 25% y-o-y to 37,000t but on a quarterly basis the figure was up by 21%, and 30% when compared with Q1. Optimism is also generated by domestic consumption in Q3 which rose by 21% sequentially to 34,000t. Although Japanese exports in Q3 were down by 31% y-o-y, they grew by 24% q-o-q to 4,000t. South Korean and Taiwanese Q3 production grew both on annual and sequential terms to 52,000t and 26,000t respectively. What is quite impressive is that South Korean exports soared by 28% q-o-q to 11,300t, which is only slightly lower compared with the same period in 2008. In addition, Taiwanese exports grew significantly in Q2 and Q3, reaching 6,100t in Q3. From a y-o-y perspective that was an aggressive growth of 65%. More than this, domestic consumption of alloy rod, bar and section expanded by 29% y-o-y to 21,000t. rates.|757.4|985.1|685.2|838.3|909.9|_915.8_| 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 10 of 12 **December 2009** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com # Industry news ### North America - The **US International Trade Commission (ITC)** unanimously decided to continue its antidumping duty investigations into imports of seamless refined copper tube from **China** and **Mexico** . The ITC has formally initiated investigations petitioned by domestic manufacturers **Cerro Flow Products** , **KobeWieland Copper Products** and two divisions of **Mueller Industries** . Preliminary determinations are due in March 2010. - **Wolverine Tube** said that net sales in Q3 2009 were US$117.9 million compared to US$216.0 million in the same period of 2008. It was reported that 45% of the decrease in net sales was due to the fall in the price of copper. But the company attributed the sales plunge primarily to low demand in its end-use sectors. The company shipped 30.2 million pounds of copper tube in Q3 2009 compared to 40.5 million pounds in Q3 2008. Wolverine Tube suffered a net loss of US$7.2 million in Q3 2009 compared to a net loss of US$23.9 million in the same period of 2008. - **Luvata** officially opened its new plant in **Monterrey** , **Mexico** . The plant engages in the production of copper commercial tube for the air conditioning and heating industry. The facility has 180,000m2 space for operations and 6,000m2 for offices; it is aiming to serve customers in Mexico and the **US** . ### Europe - **Aurubis** reported group revenue for the fiscal year ended 30th September 2009 was 6,687 million euro (US$9,736 million), compared to 8,385 million euro (US$12,207 million) for the previous year. The company said the decline was mainly due to lower

copper prices.  Gross profit for the fiscal year was 639 million euro (US$930 million), compared to 894 million euro (US$1,302 million) for the previous year, as a result of unsatisfactory business trends.  Aurubis said that it expects demand for copper products will improve in the next few months because of supportive stimulus packages and modest recovery in the end use sectors. 

- **KME** said that consolidated revenues for the nine months to September amounted to 1,396.6 million euro (US$2,054.9 million), a 42% y-o-y contraction.  Sales volumes were down by 28% y-o-y.  In the first nine months of 2009 EBITDA was 34.4 million euro (US$50.6 million) down from 94.9 million euro (US$139.7 million) in the same period of 2008.  KME commented that demand from the construction industry was weak for most of the year.  In addition, there have been some recent recovery signs in certain areas of the manufacturing sector as demand is gradually bottoming out. 

- Consolidated sales of **Halcor** in the first nine months of 2009 were 482.8 million euro (US$710.6 million) down from 938.3 million euro (US$1381.0 million) in the same period of 2008.  For the nine months to September the group suffered net losses of 19.6 million euro (US$28.8 million) compared with net losses of 16.2 million euro (US$23.8 million) a year ago. 

### North East Asia 





- **Furukawa Electric** will start operations at a rolling mill and a continuous annealing furnace for copper alloy semis in April 2010.  The new facilities are located in **Nikko** works, **Tochigi, Japan** . The rolling mill will fabricate high strength copper alloy products, featuring automatic control of thickness and shape.  Also, the continuous annealing furnace can endure temperature of 1,000 degrees Celsius, enabling the production of high-strength copper alloy semis.  The company is expecting to achieve quality improvement as well as shorter lead times.  In addition, the new facilities aim to meet the diverse needs of connector makers. 

- The **Japan Copper and Brass Association** said that output of copper and copper alloy semifinished products fell by 12% y-o-y in October to 69,218t.  It was the 15<sup>th</sup> consecutive month of decline; however, October output was the highest level and the slowest drop since last November. Demand for copper commercial tube used in air conditioners remains subdued but there is some recovery in the automotive and semiconductor sectors.

nce a copper fabricating project located in **Yingtai Industry Park** .  The investment is funded by **Fujian** merchants and amounts to 360.0 million yuan (US$52.7 million).
